newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar off earlier highs in late Tokyo trade.
newsitem.headline: Dollar off earlier highs in late Tokyo trade.

text.p: 0630 GMT TRADED HI/LO AS OF 0600 GMT

The dollar was off earlier highs against the mark and yen in late Tokyo trade on Monday, after earlier rising sharply against the German currency following a left-wing victory in Sunday's second round of French parliamentary elections.
"Several stop-losses were triggered and pushed dollar/mark sharply higher in the morning," said a city bank trader.
Stop-loss dollar buying against the mark was triggered at several points, including 1.7110 and 1.7130 marks, dealers said.

A wave of mark selling was triggered by worries that a Socialist-led government in France would lead to enlarged European economic and monetary union (EMU) membership and a weak single European currency, dealers said.
France's Socialist Party, though committed to a single European currency, is demanding a more flexible interpretation of the Maastricht Treaty and early EMU membership for Italy, Spain and Portugal.
The dollar, the British pound and the Swiss franc are expected to gain against the mark due to their safe-haven status amid uncertainties about EMU, dealers said.
The mark also lost ground against the yen on selling by Tokyo operators, including trust banks, dealers said.
The mark was quoted around 67.74/77 yen as of 0654 GMT, down from about 68.18 yen in late New York trade on Friday.

After an initial surge, the dollar was capped by talk of selling by hedge funds at 1.7150 marks, dealers said. There was also talk that the Bank of France sold the mark for the French franc at slightly below 3.3800 francs in early Asian trade.
"The dollar's upside starts looking heavier as it approaches 1.7200 marks," said a trust bank trader.
As for the dollar/yen, the market lacked fresh incentives to push it significantly in either direction, dealers said.
The U.S. currency was capped by exporters' offers above 116.50 yen but underpinned by buying interest from Japanese institutional investors below 116.00 yen, dealers said.

"If some Japanese government officials make remarks about Japanese interest rates, we might see swings in the dollar/yen. If not, the dollar/yen is likely to remain stuck in a narrow range until Friday's U.S. job report," said the bank trader.
Tokyo operators are continuing to watch Japanese interest rates, but today's activity in the Japanese government bond market provided few clues, a city bank dealer said.
The yield of the benchmark 182nd 10-year JGB was at 2.545 percent as of 0721 GMT, up just slightly from 2.535 percent on Friday.
The dollar closed at around 116.25/35 yen and 1.7056/61 marks in New York on Friday.
---Kanta Watanabe in Tokyo +81-3-3432-9780
